thread:
maya: FYI I'm starting onboard for weightpack-7b (s3://redwood-models/weightpack-7b). License file attached to the repo says 'Research-Only-NonCommercial v0.1'. Can we serve embeddings or do quant experiments for customers? cc @oliver

tom: Quick perf note — 4-bit quant build looks promising on the perf harness. I'll push benchmark numbers soon.

sasha: License wording matters a lot. 'Research-only' + NC usually rules out commercial hosting. Need legal to confirm whether serving embeddings counts as redistribution or just inference.

oliver: I'm Oliver from Legal. Do not serve commercially or redistribute weights until we review. Please attach the full license text to a PR and tag legal: we'll triage. High-level: if the license explicitly forbids commercial use, offering the model as a paid service is disallowed. If it forbids redistribution of weights but not inference, hosting may be allowed — but the "research-only"/NC combo usually blocks commercial inference as well.

maya: Clarify: is running a dedicated instance for a paying customer considered "commercial inference"?

oliver: Yes, that counts as commercial use. Even if you don't ship weights, running the model for customers is providing a commercial service.

tom: For internal experiments (non-customer), we can continue. Also FYI quant run command I'm using: `python tools/quantize.py --bits 4 --calib 500 --out q4/` — will include exact config in the PR.

sasha: Also noticed early eval regressions: ~2.3 BLEU drop on our translation test with q4. Will add diffs to the PR. If legal says no external serve, we should still run internal benching to inform options.

deploy-bot: Build started for weightpack-7b/q4 — https://ci.redwood/build/1234

oliver: Please add `LEGAL: license-review` to the PR title and include the license file and a short description of intended uses (embeddings, inference, private vs public). We'll aim for a 48h turnaround. If the upstream maintainer is open to relicensing or adding an exception, we can negotiate.

maya: Created PR #458 with license, eval logs, and quant artifacts. Tagging legal now. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
